title: Four Marian dogmas
hookLine: Mother of God, ever-virgin, Immaculate Conception, Assumption

lines: A KNOCK IN THE HILL COUNTRY.
cards: An older woman in the hill country, expecting a child she never thought she'd have, hears someone at the door. It's Mary, her kinswoman, who has hurried there.
And Elizabeth, in Luke's Gospel, cries out, in the Douay-Rheims: "And whence is this to me, that the mother of my Lord should come to me?"
Long after, the Church would sit with words like these and ask what exactly they mean. A new block begins today: Mary, her feasts, her titles and her teaching.
It starts with a word that sounds stiff and cold, and turns out to be neither: dogma.

teach.b: In the Catechism, a dogma is a truth the Church teaches as revealed by God, in a definitive way that asks for the assent of faith. It also gives a gentle picture: dogmas are lights along the path of faith, making it safe.

Four concern Mary. One: Mother of God, which you met on day eighty. A council at Ephesus affirmed for Mary the Greek title Theotokos, God-bearer, because the child she carried is one person, truly God and truly man.
The title is first about who Jesus is.
Two: ever virgin. Mary stayed a virgin before, during and after the birth of Jesus; tomorrow takes that one slowly.

Three: the Immaculate Conception. Pope Pius the Ninth taught that Mary, from the first moment of her own life, was kept free from original sin, by the grace of God and in view of what her son would do.

It's about her conception, not Jesus' birth, an easy mix-up. Four: the Assumption. Pope Pius the Twelfth taught that at the end of her earthly life Mary was taken up, body and soul, into heavenly glory.
Each one points back to Christ: who he is, how he came, what his saving work does, and where it leads. The Church sees in Mary what grace can do in one human life.

And who holds what. Orthodox Christians also call Mary Theotokos, honor her as ever virgin, and celebrate her falling asleep and her glory. Other Christians hold some of these teachings and not others.
This path describes the Catholic teaching, and ranks no one.

how: Catholics celebrate these teachings at feasts through the Church's year, including Mary, Mother of God, the Immaculate Conception and the Assumption, and the Hail Mary greets her as Mother of God.

o: a strong personal opinion held stubbornly
a truth the Church teaches as revealed by God
a church rule that can change with each pope

games.q: four Marian dogmas — tap the pairs.
p: Mary kept free from original sin
lights along the path of faith

s: the Immaculate Conception is about Jesus' birth
it's about Mary's own conception: kept free from original sin from her first moment.
the title Mother of God is first about who Jesus is
the child Mary carried is one person, truly God and truly man.
the Catechism pictures dogmas as fences
it calls them lights along the path of faith.

games.q: you're at the council at Ephesus. what do you call Mary, whose child is truly God and truly man?
o: mother of Jesus' human nature only.
no title at all, to be safe.
games.why: the council affirmed the title Theotokos, because her son is one person. the title protects a truth about Jesus first.

practice: On each slow breath, name one of the four and let a picture come with it: Mother of God, a mother holding a child; ever virgin, a closed garden gate; Immaculate Conception, a clean first page; Assumption, someone lifted home.
If one puzzles you, let it; questions are welcome. If you pray, greet Mary with Elizabeth's words, the mother of my Lord.

wordCard.voice: Dogma. A truth the Church teaches as revealed, defined so it can be held with confidence: lights along the path. Four of them concern Mary.

orig.note: Greek: a decree or settled teaching; Acts uses it for the decisions of the apostles at Jerusalem.

carryVoice: Your line: four teachings. Mother of God, ever virgin, Immaculate Conception, Assumption. Rest easy, and see you soon.
